item.title: China, France should strengthen dialogue, jointly address challenges, says FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
China, France should strengthen dialogue, jointly address challenges, says FM BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- China and France should strengthen dialogue and cooperation, consolidate political mutual trust, and jointly address various risks and challenges, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Tuesday. During a phone conversation with French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noel Barrot, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, noted that China and France are both founding members of the United Nations and permanent members of the UN Security Council. The two countries' maintaining communication and strengthening coordination on developments and changes in the international situation are important for safeguarding the international system with the United Nations at its core, Wang said. China is ready to work with France to fulfill their special responsibilities as permanent members of the UN Security Council and safeguard the common interests of the international community, he said. Maintaining the healthy and stable development of China-France relations serves the interests of both countries and the international community, Wang said, calling on both sides to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state. He expressed the hope that France would honor its commitment to the one-China principle through concrete actions and safeguard the political foundation of China-France relations. China and the European Union (EU) stand to gain from cooperation and lose from confrontation, Wang said, calling on the EU to work with China to build stable and balanced trade ties as key trading partners. Wang said he believes that France, as a core EU member state, would play a constructive role in this regard. For his part, Barrot said France has consistently attached great importance to China's status as a major country and remains committed to the one-China policy. France hopes to maintain high-level engagement with China, deepen strategic mutual trust, and strengthen communication and coordination on such major issues as UN affairs and artificial intelligence, in order to jointly uphold multilateralism, safeguard global security and stability, and promote common development and prosperity, he said. France stands ready to play an active role in fostering dialogue and cooperation between the EU and China, Barrot said. The two sides also exchanged views on other issues of common concern, including the election of UN secretary-general. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Global climate resilience faces a test as Super El Nino nears its peak
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
Global climate resilience faces a test as Super El Nino nears its peak A series of extreme weather events around the world has drawn widespread attention in recent days. Torrential rain in north and central Chile has set new weather records in a century, while the Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, has seen persistent rainfall, transforming its landscape into a carpet of flowers. Meanwhile, transboundary haze continues to spread across Southeast Asia, prompting Indonesia, Myanmar, and the Philippines to issue alerts over electricity supplies and public health. In Papua New Guinea, drought has led to the declaration of a humanitarian emergency. Behind these unusual weather events lies a common cause. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) expects the current super El Nino to peak by the end of this year, potentially reaching unprecedented intensity since systematic climate monitoring began. The current El Nino is exceptionally intense, far exceeding normal levels. El Nino, a natural climate phenomenon driven by periodic warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, typically occurs every two to seven years. But the ongoing eastern Pacific-type El Nino event, characterized by unusually warm waters concentrated in the eastern equatorial Pacific, is developing faster and is expected to reach a higher peak than any of the three previous super El Nino events. According to China's National Climate Center, sea surface temperature anomalies in the eastern Pacific have already exceeded 3 degrees Celsius. The current El Nino is forecast to reach a sea surface temperature anomaly of 3.2 to 3.5 degrees Celsius at its peak, surpassing the previous record of 2.8 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, global warming is adding to the pressure. Global average daily sea surface temperatures reached a record high in August. The UK Met Office predicts that next year is likely to be the warmest on record. The combined effects are likely to make extreme weather events more frequent and more severe. The record-breaking super El Nino poses a sweeping test of global resilience to climate impacts. As its effects ripple across the world, countries with weaker climate adaptation capacities are likely to bear heavier costs. Food security is among the areas most immediately affected. Shifts in rain belts could bring drought and sharp declines in agricultural output to rain-fed farming regions in southern Africa, Central America, and other parts of the world. The World Food Programme estimates that a strong El Nino could leave nearly 49 million more people facing severe food insecurity. The energy system also faces pressure from supply and demand. Higher temperatures drive up electricity consumption, while drought reduces hydropower generation. For many countries, this creates a difficult situation in which electricity demand peaks just as power generation declines. Public health faces growing threats as well. Smoke from forest fires in Indonesia can travel across borders, carrying fine particulate matter that harms respiratory and cardiovascular health. Academic research estimates that fires and haze during the 2015 El Nino event caused around 100,000 excess deaths. The lessons of the past remain fresh. There is now broad global consensus on how El Nino is developing and how far its impacts may reach. This is a crucial time to plan ahead and prepare for disasters. During the El Nino event in 2023-2024, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) carried out anticipatory actions in 24 countries, reaching approximately 1.7 million people. The experience showed that early intervention can help countries significantly reduce their losses. However, the lack of concrete action in global climate governance remains striking. Developed countries have fallen well behind on their pledge to provide $100 billion in climate finance annually. Technology transfer to developing countries remains constrained by numerous barriers. Many countries vulnerable to climate change are left watching as warnings of impending hazards become disasters. At its core, El Nino is a natural climate cycle. But global warming is amplifying its destructive impacts, laying bare inequalities in global climate governance. Climate risks do not stop at national borders, and no country should sit on the sidelines in addressing challenges. In the face of the super El Nino, we must seize the window for action following early warnings and take concrete measures, such as adjusting agricultural supplies, reinforcing river embankments and ensuring reliable energy supplies. We must uphold multilateralism and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, while stepping up efforts to both mitigate climate change and adapt to its impacts. Only by translating commitments into action and global consensus into tangible benefits for all can we minimize the impact of the El Nino event and safeguard our shared planet. (Li Yan is a researcher at the Faculty of Geographical Science, Beijing Normal University.) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China-CEEC forum calls for greater win-win cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
China-CEEC forum calls for greater win-win cooperation Guests attend the 6th China-Central and Eastern Europe High-Level Think Tank Scholars Forum in Sofia, Bulgaria, Nov. 9, 2026. The 6th China-Central and Eastern Europe High-Level Think Tank Scholars Forum, themed "China-Europe Dialogue: Expanding Synergies and Embracing a Win-Win Future," was held on Monday, bringing together more than 100 experts and scholars from Bulgaria, Croatia, Romania, Serbia and other countries. (Xinhua/Zhou Hailun) SOFIA, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- The 6th China-Central and Eastern Europe High-Level Think Tank Scholars Forum, themed "China-Europe Dialogue: Expanding Synergies and Embracing a Win-Win Future," was held on Monday, bringing together more than 100 experts and scholars from Bulgaria, Croatia, Romania, Serbia and other countries. Wang Junwei, director of the Academic and Editorial Committee of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, said in his keynote speech that seeking common ground while preserving differences and pursuing cooperation for mutual benefit are important principles guiding China's approach to international relations and valuable experience in ensuring the steady development of China-Europe relations. These principles will continue to play a guiding role in cooperation between China and Central and Eastern European countries (CEEC) in the future, he said. In her welcome remarks, Chinese Ambassador to Bulgaria Dai Qingli said that as long as China and Europe uphold mutual respect and engage in equal-footed consultations, both sides will be able to find solutions to problems and continuously expand the scope for mutually beneficial cooperation. Nataliya Kiselova, former president of the National Assembly of Bulgaria, said in her remarks that the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC demonstrated the CPC leadership's courage to uphold the truth and curb abuses of power, and its determination to continue consolidating its position as the core of leadership in Chinese society. Wu Haitao, vice president of the China Public Diplomacy Association, said that think-tank exchanges serve as an important channel for continuously strengthening the public-opinion foundation of China-Europe friendship. Participants held in-depth discussions on China's 15th Five-Year Plan, the four major global initiatives, global governance, and the prospects and vision for China-EU relations. The inaugural forum was held in 2016. Since then, it has played an active role in facilitating exchanges of ideas and building consensus among think-tank scholars from China and CEEC. This year's forum was jointly organized by the Scientific Research Planning Department of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the Chinese Embassy in Bulgaria, the China Public Diplomacy Association, the Bulgaria National Association for the Belt and Road, and Sofia University. item.title: China makes breakthroughs in underground navigation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
China makes breakthroughs in underground navigation Photo shows the State Key Laboratory of Integrated Space-Time Networks and Equipment Technology under the 54th Research Institute of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC54). (Photo/Zhang Yue) "I no longer have to drive around aimlessly looking for a parking space underground. With navigation, I can now see at a glance which parking spaces are available on each level," said Chen Chong, an engineer at the 54th Research Institute of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC54), at the underground parking lot of Xiong'an Science Park in Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei province. As Chen taps "park" on a navigation app called "Xingyuan," the total number of parking spaces, the number of available spaces, and their exact locations are displayed immediately. After he selects a space, the navigation route extends from above ground to underground, guiding him through the entrance, ramps, and junctions straight to his destination. Traditional navigation in underground parking lots has long faced three challenges: satellite signals cannot penetrate underground structures, ordinary smartphones cannot provide accurate positioning, and navigation guidance is not continuous. The technology behind the intelligent underground parking navigation service used by Chen is the "Xingyuan" BeiDou micro-base-station system for underground positioning and navigation, developed by a team at the State Key Laboratory of Integrated Space-Time Networks and Equipment Technology under CETC54. The high-precision positioning, navigation, and control technology for large underground spaces, developed by the team, marks a major original breakthrough by China in integrated space-time networks for underground environments. Yu Baoguo, director of the laboratory and head of the project, explained that by deploying BeiDou micro base stations in underground parking lots to transmit BeiDou signals, the team has overcome key technical challenges in intelligent network deployment and seamless positioning and navigation between aboveground and underground spaces, making it possible for ordinary smartphones to use positioning and navigation services underground. Underground spaces encompass not only familiar places such as parking lots, but also complex underground logistics corridors and utility tunnels. The "Xingyuan" system makes applications such as personnel inspections, group work management, and unmanned logistics possible. When inspection personnel enter hazardous areas, the system issues alerts. Unmanned transport vehicles can travel steadily and stop accurately in underground passages where satellite signals are unavailable. "Field tests of the independently developed underground positioning and navigation system show that it can achieve static positioning accuracy of better than 0.2 meters for people in underground spaces, and enable high-speed autonomous vehicles to navigate reliably with sub-meter accuracy," Chen said. At Menkeqing Coal Mine in Ordos, north China's Inner Mongolia autonomous region, a miner carries a smartphone designed for use in mines walks from the surface down into the mine. As he moves through intersecting tunnels, the system not only shows which tunnel he is in but also accurately identifies his underground level and elevation. Positioning remains continuous and stable even in areas crowded with metal equipment, such as working faces and pump rooms. When he needs to reach another work site, the miner can simply use his phone to request a ride. Based on his location, the system dispatches an unmanned shuttle vehicle, which autonomously follows a planned route through junctions and bends before arriving precisely at the designated locations for pick-up and drop-off. "Behind this is the integrated space-time network our team has deployed in underground coal mines. It enables the continuous display of personnel and vehicle positions in three-dimensional space, extending BeiDou positioning from the surface to underground areas. Mining vehicles are also equipped with precise autonomous navigation and control capabilities," said Du Shitong, the team's head of system integration technology. Du added that the system is also equipped with a digital management platform for coal mining operations, providing technical support for the intelligent transformation of the coal industry. Core chips are essential to underground positioning and navigation. Before the project was launched in 2022, China relied on imported core ultra-wideband (UWB) positioning chips. They were costly, supply chains were unstable, and core technologies and standards were controlled by foreign companies. To address this, the team pursued fundamental innovation in signal standards, developing its own HNav-UWB signal standard. This marks a fundamental shift from the traditional design approach, which prioritizes communications over positioning, to a new paradigm that gives priority to positioning, with communications playing a supporting role. "Comprehensive testing and verification show that, compared with internationally adopted standards, the new standard extends coverage by 28 percent, improves ranging accuracy by 6 percent and increases single-station capacity by more than 65 percent. Its core performance indicators outperform those of leading international standards across the board," said Yang Menghuan, who leads the design of the HNav-UWB signal standard. Based on the HNav-UWB standard, China has successfully developed the "Tanjie 100," the country's first domestically developed and independently controllable pulse-positioning chip. "The chip delivers ultra-high positioning accuracy comparable to that of BeiDou navigation above ground, fundamentally addressing the problems of positioning ambiguity and large errors associated with conventional underground positioning systems," said Zhao Jun, head of chip development. In the future, the development and utilization of underground spaces will enter a new stage characterized by large-scale, intelligent and systematic development, while demand for ubiquitous, high-precision space-time information services will continue to grow. "We will continue to focus on integrated space-time networks, further improve the performance of core technologies and equipment, and expand their applications. We will also promote the large-scale deployment of these technologies in more fields, including urban underground utility tunnels, subway tunnels, deep mines and underground civil air defense facilities, establishing 'Chinese standards' for the intelligent development of underground spaces worldwide and providing strong support for high-quality economic and social development," said Yu. item.title: China's import expo tells a larger story of openness, shared opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
China's import expo tells a larger story of openness, shared opportunities SHANGHAI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- In 2018, German warehouse-equipment maker Jungheinrich showcased a German-made forklift at China's inaugural import expo. This year, it unveiled an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted warehouse-planning tool developed partly in China -- a sign of the country's growing role as a source of innovation for global businesses, not just a vast market. The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday, attracted a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors and featured more than 480 global, Asian or China debuts. Organizers reported 85.45 billion U.S. dollars in intended deals. For decades, China's manufacturing strengths have drawn foreign companies, many of which have used the country as a base to serve global markets. In 2025, foreign-invested enterprises accounted for 27 percent of China's exports and 16 percent of its trade surplus, according to official figures. Shanghai has long been a major gateway for China's exports. In 2025, its port recorded total container throughput of more than 55 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), retaining its position as the world's busiest container port for the 16th consecutive year. The city has also become a gateway for foreign businesses seeking access to China's import market. Since 2018, it has hosted the CIIE, the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, described by Chinese officials as "an international public good shared by the world." For Ethiopian economist Alemayehu Geda, China's expanding import market offers an opportunity for African producers to move beyond raw-material exports. China is "not only encouraging exporters as was traditionally the case, but also importers into China," the Addis Ababa University professor said. Greek financial news outlet Business Daily described the CIIE as an "importathon" -- a blend of "import" and "marathon," suggesting a sustained drive to bring goods into the Chinese market. Nepalese entrepreneur Shankar Koirala has witnessed those opportunities grow over six CIIE appearances. His booth expanded from nine to 72 square meters. Each handmade cashmere scarf bears its maker's signature. Together, the products connect Chinese buyers with more than 600 artisan families in Nepal. "When we didn't know where to promote our products, the CIIE gave us a platform," Koirala said. John Ross, a former director of economic and business policy for the mayor of London, told Xinhua that China was not seeking a trade surplus but rather greater openness in world trade. For foreign exporters, he called the CIIE "the best export opportunity that you've got in the world." This photo taken on Nov. 4, 2026 shows a view of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue for the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua/Chen Haoming) China imported more than 90 trillion yuan (about 13.4 trillion U.S. dollars) worth of goods between 2021 and 2025. At this year's CIIE, free exhibition space for the least developed countries increased by 17 percent, while the Asia-Africa products zone was upgraded. Beyond the exhibition halls, China has expanded preferential access to its market. Since May 1, eligible imports from all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations have enjoyed zero tariffs. That morning, 24 tonnes of South African apples became the first shipment cleared under the policy in Shenzhen. When China joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001, its annual goods trade stood at about 500 billion U.S. dollars. By 2025, it exceeded 6 trillion dollars. China's role as a buyer has grown as well: imports from more than 130 countries and regions increased last year, customs data showed. China has also taken steps in support of the multilateral trading system. In 2025, it announced it would not seek new special and differential treatment in current or future WTO negotiations. This year, it pledged 1.1 million dollars to WTO programs that support developing and least-developed economies. These efforts come as the multilateral trading system faces mounting challenges. The WTO's World Trade Report 2026 says global trade policy and the organization face "the most serious and sustained disruptions" since the multilateral trading system emerged 80 years ago. Addressing the opening ceremony of the CIIE, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called on countries to share market opportunities and promote balanced trade by making the economic pie bigger together. He also urged deeper investment cooperation, innovation and the removal of trade barriers. This photo taken on April 1, 2026 shows the phase IV automated terminal of Shanghai Yangshan Deep Water Port in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua/Cheng Li) For French yeast maker Lesaffre, making that pie bigger through innovation can bring benefits well beyond China. At its Shanghai industrial baking center, the company tests processes for customers across Asia-Pacific. Solutions refined in China can be applied elsewhere, an approach the company calls the "China fulcrum effect." "A solution validated on these lines in China can be scaled for customers across Asia-Pacific," said Jérôme Vanachter, president of Lesaffre Greater China. In cosmetics, French group L'Oréal joined forces with Chinese company Nanomed to develop a Lancome skincare device. Displayed at the 2025 CIIE, the device had reached markets in more than 20 countries and regions by July 2026. In telecommunications, U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm showcased a sixth-generation (6G) communications terminal prototype following tests with China Mobile and Chinese telecommunications equipment maker ZTE. The CIIE also served as a platform for emerging innovators. This year's innovation incubation section featured 633 projects from nearly 40 countries and regions, up almost 20 percent from the previous edition. Taken together, these examples point to an evolution beyond unveiling imported products and technologies. International companies are increasingly developing new technologies and manufacturing innovative products in China, drawing on local expertise to serve both Chinese and overseas markets -- part of what has come to be known as "China Opportunity 2.0." Representatives of enterprises and organizations for the 10th China International Import Expo (CIIE) pose for a group photo during the ninth CIIE Culture Night event and the signing ceremony of the 10th CIIE at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) in Shanghai, east China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Fang Zhe) Shanghai's own history offers a wider perspective on this evolution. The city became home to China's first pilot free trade zone in 2013. This July, representatives of 29 countries signed an agreement in Shanghai to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, which will be headquartered in the city. China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China next week. The theme of this year's summit is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," while China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC cooperation. In 2025, APEC's 21 member economies were home to 3 billion people and accounted for 61.6 percent of global real GDP. The gathering carries historical resonance. Shanghai hosted APEC leaders in October 2001, just weeks before China's WTO accession, at a meeting that marked a fresh start for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the new century. At the 2014 Beijing summit, leaders endorsed a roadmap toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, an initiative that APEC trade ministers reaffirmed their commitment to advancing in May. Back in Shanghai, 49 companies and institutions signed up on Nov. 6 for the CIIE's 10th edition in 2027. Among them was German optics group ZEISS, which this year showcased a new-generation intraocular lens developed by its joint venture in China. For Martin Fischer, president and CEO of ZEISS Greater China, China is not only the company's largest market globally, but also a vital source of innovation. "The time it takes to turn an idea into a prototype is shorter in China than anywhere else," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Working together to protect the ocean and promote sustainable prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
Working together to protect the ocean and promote sustainable prosperity Photo shows an aerial view of Gulangyu Island in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian province. (Photo/Wang Chu) Addressing the governance deficit of the high seas has become a shared challenge for humanity. The ocean has given rise to life, connected the world, and driven development. Yet the high seas, which account for two-thirds of the world's oceans, have long been inadequately governed, with less than 1 percent of their area effectively protected. In January this year, the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) entered into force, ushering in a new chapter in global ocean governance. As one of the first countries to sign the agreement and become a Party to it, China participated extensively in the negotiations throughout the process and has applied to host the agreement's secretariat in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian province. The 2026 World Ocean Week in Xiamen, themed "Safeguard the Deep Blue Together, Foster Human-Ocean Harmony," was held from November 5 to 11 in Xiamen. The coastal city is emerging as a new platform for multilateral dialogue on ocean affairs. China has a mainland coastline of approximately 18,000 kilometers and a long history of developing and utilizing marine resources. Xiamen's experience in coastal and bay management offers a vivid example of the country's efforts to promote sustainable ocean development and harmony between man and the ocean. With its livable environment and favorable business climate, Xiamen has earned international recognition as an "International Garden City." The city's comprehensive management of Yundang Lake has provided an effective model for sustainable development in coastal cities. Rare species such as Chinese white dolphins and blue-tailed bee-eaters have found habitats and breeding grounds in waters close to the city. Local efforts reflect a broader national commitment. From the adoption of China's Ocean Agenda 21 to guide the sustainable development of its marine sector, to the first revision of the Marine Environment Protection Law to strengthen the legal framework for marine environmental regulation, and then the strategic plan announced at the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) to step up efforts to build China into a strong maritime country, China has consistently incorporated marine ecological conservation into its overall approach to ocean development. The country's sustained conservation efforts have contributed to the steady recovery of marine biodiversity. China has established 353 marine protected areas, covering approximately 93,300 square kilometers of sea area, and designated around 150,000 square kilometers of marine areas as ecological red lines. Twenty-four typical marine ecosystems have remained out of the "unhealthy" category for five consecutive years. Key species, including Chinese white dolphins, sea turtles, spotted seals, and corals, have received effective protection. Populations of the Chinese horseshoe crab, often described as a "living fossil," have shown signs of recovery, while the area of mangrove forests continues to expand. China is also working to safeguard marine resources and promote a greener marine economy. It has adopted marine resource conservation measures such as expanding stock enhancement and releasing programs, implementing voluntary fishing moratoriums, and strictly fulfilling its obligations under the Agreement on Port State Measures. At the same time, the country is accelerating the development of marine renewable energy, including offshore wind and tidal power, and building a green shipping system. Migratory birds fly over Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay national marine park in Qingdao, east China's Shandong province. (Photo/Wang Haibin) China was among the first to introduce voluntary fishing moratoriums on the high seas and has strengthened controls on distant-water fishing vessels, contributing to global efforts to conserve and manage high seas fisheries resources through concrete actions. As all countries share the same blue planet, their security and well-being are closely interconnected. Focusing on the practical needs of various countries, particularly developing nations, China has placed capacity building at the center of its international cooperation on marine affairs, seeking to ensure that the benefits of development are shared more broadly and equitably by people of all countries. In Pacific island countries, China has supported the implementation of a "marine spatial planning plus" demonstration project on Malake Island and in the historical port town of Levuka, on Ovalau Island, Fiji, helping local communities address the challenge of balancing ecological conservation with economic development. In Southeast and South Asia, China has shared its experience in beach restoration, developed in Xiamen, with Thailand and Sri Lanka, and provided mangrove ecosystem restoration technologies to Cambodia. In Africa, China has helped countries including Uganda and Kenya expand their blue economies by sharing new fishing gear, advanced fishing techniques, and solutions for coastal aquaculture. Deep-sea scientific exploration and the sharing of scientific research resources are important global marine public goods that China provides to the international community. Recently, China's research vessel Deep Sea No. 1, carrying the country's manned deep-sea submersible Jiaolong, departed from Xiamen for the second leg of China's 100th oceanographic expedition, with scientists from South Pacific island countries invited to participate. Meanwhile, the ports of Shanghai, Hamburg, and Los Angeles are working together to establish green shipping corridors and advance the low-carbon transition of maritime transport. Business representatives discuss cooperation in marine equipment at the fourth Fujian International Maritime Equipment Expo in Fuzhou, southeast China's Fujian province, October 17. (Photo/Xie Guiming) China and Egypt have also collaborated on marine archaeology and the protection of underwater cultural heritage, further broadening the scope of marine cooperation. China has released the Blue Partnership Principles and launched the Sustainable Blue Partnership Cooperation Network and the Blue Partnership Action Fund. It has signed marine cooperation agreements with more than 50 countries and international organizations. Through initiatives such as the Blue Talent Program and the Marine Scholarship of China, China has also organized more than 300 capacity-building training sessions on ocean governance, training over 6,000 marine professionals and sharing practical experience with developing countries in ecological restoration, climate response, and marine planning. Firmly upholding the international system with the United Nations (UN) at its core and fully participating in the formulation and implementation of international rules on ocean affairs constitute China's consistent position in global ocean governance. Under the framework of the UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (2021-2030), China has launched major scientific programs, including the Digital Deep-sea Typical Habitats Program, and opened access to research expedition resources for developing countries, creating more opportunities for countries of the Global South to participate in international ocean science collaboration. As global ocean governance enters a new phase, China will remain committed to the vision of building a maritime community with a shared future. It will work with countries around the world to protect the blue planet and promote sustainable development, striving together toward a future of harmony between man and the ocean and shared prosperity. item.title: Belt and Road think tank cooperation, int'l communication forums start in China's Xi'an
item.description:

Belt and Road think tank cooperation, int'l communication forums start in China's Xi'an Participants are pictured during the Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 and the 4th Silk Road (Xi'an) International Communication Forum in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Nov. 10, 2026. The forum opened in Xi'an, capital city of northwest China's Shaanxi Province, on Tuesday. Themed "High-quality Belt and Road Cooperation Empowering Modernization and Mutual Learning among Civilizations," these forums aim to pool global wisdom and promote new development of Belt and Road cooperation with higher quality and at a higher level. (Xinhua/Li Yibo) XI'AN, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- The Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 and the 4th Silk Road (Xi'an) International Communication Forum opened in Xi'an, capital city of northwest China's Shaanxi Province, on Tuesday. Themed "High-quality Belt and Road Cooperation Empowering Modernization and Mutual Learning among Civilizations," these forums aim to pool global wisdom and promote new development of Belt and Road cooperation with higher quality and at a higher level. More than 300 diplomats, think tank experts, journalists, cultural and tourism experts, and business representatives from over 50 countries and regions are attending these forums to engage in exchanges and discussions. In his address, Zhao Gang, deputy secretary of the Shaanxi Provincial Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and governor of Shaanxi, said Shaanxi has in recent years deeply integrated itself into the broader pattern of Belt and Road cooperation. Lyu Yansong, editor-in-chief of Xinhua News Agency, said that over the past 13 years, Belt and Road cooperation has grown from a vision into tangible and visible cooperation projects, making positive contributions to enhancing friendship between China and partner countries and promoting the economic and social development of partner countries. As the lead of the Initiators Council of the Belt and Road Studies Network (BRSN), Xinhua is ready to work with domestic and international colleagues to deepen research and interpretation of the connotations of high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, showcase the fruitful achievements of partner countries in advancing modernization and mutual learning among civilizations, and gather strong momentum for high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, Lyu said. The BRSN has continued to expand its influence since its establishment seven years ago. At the opening ceremony, four new member institutions, namely BRICS International Forum, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Manas National Academy of the Kyrgyz Republic, and the Development Strategy Centre, Uzbekistan were presented with signing documents. A think tank report titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation" was, meanwhile, released globally in both Chinese and English. The forums are co-hosted by Xinhua News Agency, the CPC Shaanxi Provincial Committee and the Shaanxi Provincial People's Government. item.title: CIIE highlights China's long-term commitment to opening-up and development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
CIIE highlights China's long-term commitment to opening-up and development Photo shows the booth of Dole, a leading company in the fruit industry, at the agricultural and food products exhibition area at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai. (People's Daily Online/Weng Qiyu) The 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) was held from Nov. 5 to Nov. 10 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) in east China's Shanghai. Now in its ninth edition, the just-concluded CIIE continued to demonstrate its strong appeal, with several key indicators, including exhibition scale, quality, and participation, reaching new highs. A total of 162 countries, regions, and international organizations took part in the 9th CIIE, which attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors. The total exhibition area exceeded 440,000 square meters for the first time, while the number of Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders participating surpassed 300. By gathering for this annual event, the international community is expressing its confidence in China. One of the reasons the CIIE has continued to retain its appeal over the years is its commitment to long-term development. A long-term vision means staying committed to doing the right things amid uncertainty. The CIIE has consistently sent a clear message to the world: China remains committed to stable cooperation and shared development over the long term. This sense of certainty is built on the joint efforts and shared commitment of the host country, exhibitors, and other stakeholders. First, China remains firmly committed to sharing opportunities with the world. Over the years, the CIIE has been held as scheduled, consistently championing cooperation and opening-up. The first eight editions have delivered remarkable results in opening-up, attracting more than 180 countries, regions, and international organizations. Overseas exhibitors have made about 27,000 appearances at its business exhibitions. More than 3,400 representative new products, technologies, and services have made their debuts at the expo. The CIIE has become a platform for advancing high-level opening-up and an international public good shared by the world. "The Chinese market is such a big one that you should all come and see what it has to offer." This remark made by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the opening ceremony of the second CIIE is a promise that China has continued to uphold year after year. A visitor views the Halcyon Evolve intelligent ring-gantry radiotherapy platform by Siemens Healthineers. The product makes its global debut at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai. (People's Daily Online/Weng Qiyu) Second, foreign enterprises have enduring confidence in the Chinese market. This year, 169 companies and 30 overseas exhibition organizers mark their 9th consecutive participation in the CIIE. Their confidence stems not only from their past success in the Chinese market, but also from their expectations for China's long-term development prospects. Many have been deeply rooted in China for decades. The advantages of the Chinese market that continue to attract them to expand their investment have long shifted from cost advantages to innovation-driven growth. The CIIE serves as a window for foreign enterprises to observe the Chinese market and a platform for connecting with local industries. Integration and joint development have become increasingly important to the growth strategies of foreign enterprises in China. For Global South countries and small and medium-sized enterprises, the CIIE has demonstrated the vast possibilities offered by China's enormous market. From starting with a booth of just a few square meters to securing exhibition space spanning dozens of square meters and eventually opening physical stores, the inspiring stories of exhibitors of Peruvian alpaca products, Syrian traditional soaps and other goods have encouraged more businesses to move beyond short-term participation toward long-term operations in China. Third, the CIIE continues to evolve and improve. Over its first eight editions, the CIIE has kept pace with industrial development, technological advances and people's needs. Its exhibition areas have become increasingly specialized, while the exhibition experience has become smoother and business matchmaking more efficient. The platform's functions have become more comprehensive. The 9th CIIE has introduced further measures. The three brand activities, namely "Shop in China," "Export to China" and "Invest in China," are brought together to reinforce one another. For the first time, a handbook of facilitation measures for the 9th CIIE has been compiled, covering issues of particular concern to businesses, including trade, investment, customs and taxation. A number of pilot measures, including a preferred cross-border e-commerce platform and reduced fees for oversized cargo transportation, are being introduced at the expo. Support and services for the six major exhibition areas of the Business Exhibition have expanded beyond basic booth operations to cover more aspects of the exhibition process, providing greater convenience and added value for exhibitors and visitors alike. The CIIE itself has become a testing ground for opening-up policies. Visitors explore the booth of Japanese chemical giant Toray Industries at the Intelligent Industry & Information Technology exhibition area of the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai. (People's Daily Online/Weng Qiyu) Fourth, the CIIE's spillover effects continue to grow in scope and depth. The CIIE has not only provided a platform for first-time exhibitions and product launches, but also helped foster the debut economy and turn facilitation measures for the expo into regular policies. In addition to introducing new products and technologies, the expo also promotes supply chain integration, industrial chain extension and improvements to rules and institutions. The commitment to ensuring the continued success of the CIIE has been incorporated into China's top-level planning, providing institutional support for the platform's functions. The CIIE has evolved from an annual exhibition into a regular institutional arrangement and long-term policy instrument under China's national opening-up strategy. "The CIIE, which will be held on an annual basis, will feature good performance, fruitful results and continued success in the years to come." Xi's remark at the opening ceremony of the first CIIE reflects China's firm resolve and long-term vision to advance high-level opening-up. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Book of Xi's discourses on poverty reduction, alleviation published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
Book of Xi's discourses on poverty reduction, alleviation published BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A compilation of discourses by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on poverty reduction and alleviation has been published by the Central Party Literature Press and released nationwide. Compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the book brings together 55 important articles by Xi on poverty reduction and alleviation. Some of these works are made public for the first time. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core has placed poverty alleviation high on its governance agenda and regarded it as the bottom line task in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. China has won a complete victory in the fight against poverty and accomplished the arduous task of eliminating absolute poverty, creating a miracle in the human history of poverty reduction. In the process, the country has blazed a poverty reduction path and formed an anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics. Xi's discourses on poverty reduction and alleviation represent an important theoretical achievement in China's poverty alleviation efforts and the latest achievement in adapting Marxist anti-poverty theory to the Chinese context. These discourses provide important guidance for consolidating and expanding the achievements in poverty alleviation and advancing rural revitalization across the board, promoting modernization that delivers common prosperity for all, and building a better world free from poverty and featuring shared prosperity.
